def svg_line_chart(data_series, width=700, height=320, title='', colors=None, x_label='', y_label='',
                   y_format='auto', show_legend=True):
    """Multi-line SVG chart. data_series = {label: [(x, y), ...]}"""
    if colors is None:
        colors = ['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#dc2626', '#d97706', '#7c3aed', '#0891b2']

    pad_left = 75
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 55
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    all_x = sorted(set(x for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts))
    all_y = [y for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts]

    if not all_x or not all_y:
        return ''

    x_min, x_max = min(all_x), max(all_x)
    y_min_raw, y_max_raw = min(all_y), max(all_y)
    y_padding = (y_max_raw - y_min_raw) * 0.1 or y_max_raw * 0.1
    y_min = y_min_raw - y_padding
    y_max = y_max_raw + y_padding

    def px(x_val):
        if x_max == x_min:
            return pad_left + chart_w / 2
        return pad_left + (x_val - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * chart_w

    def py(y_val):
        if y_max == y_min:
            return pad_top + chart_h / 2
        return pad_top + (1 - (y_val - y_min) / (y_max - y_min)) * chart_h

    # Y grid lines
    n_grid = 5
    grid_lines = ''
    y_labels_svg = ''
    for i in range(n_grid + 1):
        y_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / n_grid
        y_pos = py(y_val)
        grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
        if y_format == 'pct':
            label = f'{y_val:.1f}%'
        elif y_format == 'usd':
            label = f'${y_val/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'k':
            label = f'{y_val/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'M':
            label = f'{y_val/1e6:.1f}M'
        else:
            label = f'{y_val:.2f}' if y_val < 10 else f'{int(y_val):,}'
        y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{label}</text>'

    # X axis labels
    x_labels_svg = ''
    step = max(1, len(all_x) // 8)
    for i, x_val in enumerate(all_x):
        if i % step == 0 or x_val == all_x[-1]:
            x_pos = px(x_val)
            x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_pos:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+20}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{x_val}</text>'

    # Lines
    paths = ''
    for idx, (label, pts) in enumerate(data_series.items()):
        color = colors[idx % len(colors)]
        pts_sorted = sorted(pts, key=lambda p: p[0])
        d = ' '.join(f'{"M" if i==0 else "L"}{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for i, (x, y) in enumerate(pts_sorted))
        paths += f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{color}" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
        # Dots at each point
        for x, y in pts_sorted:
            paths += f'<circle cx="{px(x):.1f}" cy="{py(y):.1f}" r="3" fill="{color}"/>'

    # Legend
    legend_svg = ''
    if show_legend and len(data_series) > 1:
        lx = pad_left
        for idx, label in enumerate(data_series.keys()):
            color = colors[idx % len(colors)]
            legend_svg += f'''<rect x="{lx}" y="{height-18}" width="12" height="12" fill="{color}" rx="2"/>
            <text x="{lx+16}" y="{height-7}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{label}</text>'''
            lx += len(label) * 7 + 30

    # Title
    title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

    return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {paths}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="{pad_left}" y="{height-4}" font-size="10" fill="#9ca3af">{x_label}</text>
</svg>'''


def svg_bar_chart(labels, values, width=700, height=320, title='', color='#2563eb',
                  colors=None, y_format='auto', horizontal=False, show_values=True):
    """Single-series bar chart."""
    pad_left = 75 if not horizontal else 150
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 70
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    n = len(labels)
    if n == 0:
        return ''

    y_max = max(values) * 1.15
    y_min = 0

    bar_colors = colors or [color] * n

    def fmt_val(v):
        if y_format == 'pct':
            return f'{v:.1f}%'
        elif y_format == 'usd':
            return f'${v/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'k':
            return f'{v/1000:.1f}K'
        elif y_format == 'M':
            return f'{v/1e6:.1f}M'
        elif y_format == 'score':
            return f'{v:.1f}'
        else:
            return f'{v:.2f}' if v < 10 else f'{int(v):,}'

    if not horizontal:
        bar_w = chart_w / n * 0.6
        gap = chart_w / n

        bars = ''
        x_labels_svg = ''
        for i, (lbl, val) in enumerate(zip(labels, values)):
            x_center = pad_left + gap * i + gap / 2
            bar_h = (val - y_min) / (y_max - y_min) * chart_h if y_max > y_min else 0
            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h - bar_h
            bars += f'<rect x="{x_center - bar_w/2:.1f}" y="{y_pos:.1f}" width="{bar_w:.1f}" height="{bar_h:.1f}" fill="{bar_colors[i % len(bar_colors)]}" rx="3"/>'
            if show_values:
                bars += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{y_pos - 4:.1f}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{fmt_val(val)}</text>'
            # X labels - wrap long labels
            lbl_str = str(lbl)
            if len(lbl_str) > 12:
                words = lbl_str.split()
                if len(words) > 1:
                    mid = len(words) // 2
                    line1 = ' '.join(words[:mid])
                    line2 = ' '.join(words[mid:])
                    x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#6b7280">{line1}</text>'
                    x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+29}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#6b7280">{line2}</text>'
                else:
                    x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#6b7280">{lbl_str[:14]}</text>'
            else:
                x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{lbl}</text>'

        # Y grid
        grid_lines = ''
        y_labels_svg = ''
        for i in range(6):
            y_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / 5
            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h * (1 - i / 5)
            grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
            y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{fmt_val(y_val)}</text>'

        title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

        return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {bars}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''
    else:
        # horizontal
        bar_h = chart_h / n * 0.6
        gap = chart_h / n
        bars = ''
        y_labels_svg = ''
        for i, (lbl, val) in enumerate(zip(labels, values)):
            y_center = pad_top + gap * i + gap / 2
            bar_len = (val / y_max) * chart_w if y_max > 0 else 0
            bars += f'<rect x="{pad_left}" y="{y_center - bar_h/2:.1f}" width="{bar_len:.1f}" height="{bar_h:.1f}" fill="{bar_colors[i % len(bar_colors)]}" rx="3"/>'
            if show_values:
                bars += f'<text x="{pad_left + bar_len + 5:.1f}" y="{y_center + 4:.1f}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{fmt_val(val)}</text>'
            lbl_str = str(lbl)[:22]
            y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left - 6}" y="{y_center + 4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{lbl_str}</text>'

        # X grid
        grid_lines = ''
        x_labels_svg_h = ''
        for i in range(6):
            x_val = y_max * i / 5
            x_pos = pad_left + (x_val / y_max) * chart_w if y_max > 0 else pad_left
            grid_lines += f'<line x1="{x_pos:.1f}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{x_pos:.1f}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
            x_labels_svg_h += f'<text x="{x_pos:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{fmt_val(x_val)}</text>'

        title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

        return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {bars}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg_h}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''


def svg_grouped_bar(groups, series_data, width=700, height=340, title='', colors=None, y_format='auto'):
    """Grouped bar chart. series_data = {series_name: [values per group]}"""
    if colors is None:
        colors = ['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#dc2626', '#d97706', '#7c3aed']

    pad_left = 75
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 65
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    n_groups = len(groups)
    n_series = len(series_data)
    all_vals = [v for vals in series_data.values() for v in vals]
    y_max = max(all_vals) * 1.15 if all_vals else 1
    y_min = 0

    group_w = chart_w / n_groups
    bar_w = group_w * 0.7 / n_series

    def fmt_val(v):
        if y_format == 'pct':
            return f'{v:.0f}%'
        elif y_format == 'usd':
            return f'${v/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'k':
            return f'{v/1000:.1f}K'
        else:
            return f'{v:.2f}' if v < 10 else f'{int(v):,}'

    bars = ''
    x_labels_svg = ''
    for gi, group in enumerate(groups):
        group_center = pad_left + group_w * gi + group_w / 2
        for si, (sname, vals) in enumerate(series_data.items()):
            val = vals[gi]
            color = colors[si % len(colors)]
            bar_h = (val / y_max) * chart_h if y_max > 0 else 0
            x_pos = group_center - (n_series / 2 * bar_w) + si * bar_w
            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h - bar_h
            bars += f'<rect x="{x_pos:.1f}" y="{y_pos:.1f}" width="{bar_w:.1f}" height="{bar_h:.1f}" fill="{color}" rx="2"/>'

        lbl = str(group)
        x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{group_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{lbl}</text>'

    # Y grid
    grid_lines = ''
    y_labels_svg = ''
    for i in range(6):
        y_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / 5
        y_pos = pad_top + chart_h * (1 - i / 5)
        grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
        y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{fmt_val(y_val)}</text>'

    # Legend
    legend_svg = ''
    lx = pad_left
    for si, (sname, _) in enumerate(series_data.items()):
        color = colors[si % len(colors)]
        legend_svg += f'''<rect x="{lx}" y="{height-18}" width="12" height="12" fill="{color}" rx="2"/>
        <text x="{lx+16}" y="{height-7}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{sname}</text>'''
        lx += len(sname) * 7 + 30

    title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

    return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {bars}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''


def svg_stacked_area(data_series, width=700, height=320, title='', colors=None, y_format='pct', x_label=''):
    """Stacked area chart. data_series = {label: [(x, y), ...]} where y are proportions."""
    if colors is None:
        colors = ['#dc2626', '#d97706', '#16a34a']

    pad_left = 60
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 55
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    all_x = sorted(set(x for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts))
    if not all_x:
        return ''
    x_min, x_max = min(all_x), max(all_x)

    def px(x_val):
        if x_max == x_min:
            return pad_left + chart_w / 2
        return pad_left + (x_val - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * chart_w

    # Build stacked values
    series_names = list(data_series.keys())
    # For each x, get cumulative sums
    x_vals_map = defaultdict(dict)
    for sname, pts in data_series.items():
        for x, y in pts:
            x_vals_map[x][sname] = y

    paths_svg = ''
    for si, sname in enumerate(series_names):
        color = colors[si % len(colors)]
        # compute bottom and top stacks
        top_pts = []
        bot_pts = []
        for x in all_x:
            cum_top = sum(x_vals_map[x].get(s, 0) for s in series_names[:si+1])
            cum_bot = sum(x_vals_map[x].get(s, 0) for s in series_names[:si])
            top_pts.append((x, cum_top))
            bot_pts.append((x, cum_bot))

        def py(y_val):
            return pad_top + (1 - y_val / 100) * chart_h

        # Forward top, backward bottom
        forward = ' '.join(f'{"M" if i==0 else "L"}{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for i, (x, y) in enumerate(top_pts))
        backward = ' '.join(f'L{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for x, y in reversed(bot_pts))
        d = f'{forward} {backward} Z'
        paths_svg += f'<path d="{d}" fill="{color}" opacity="0.8"/>'

    # Y labels
    y_labels_svg = ''
    grid_lines = ''
    for i in range(6):
        y_val = i * 20
        y_pos = pad_top + chart_h * (1 - y_val / 100)
        grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
        y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{y_val}%</text>'

    # X labels
    x_labels_svg = ''
    step = max(1, len(all_x) // 8)
    for i, x_val in enumerate(all_x):
        if i % step == 0 or x_val == all_x[-1]:
            x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{px(x_val):.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+20}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{x_val}</text>'

    # Legend
    legend_svg = ''
    lx = pad_left
    for si, sname in enumerate(series_names):
        color = colors[si % len(colors)]
        legend_svg += f'''<rect x="{lx}" y="{height-18}" width="12" height="12" fill="{color}" rx="2" opacity="0.8"/>
        <text x="{lx+16}" y="{height-7}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{sname}</text>'''
        lx += len(sname) * 7 + 30

    title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

    return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {paths_svg}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''

def table_html(headers, rows, caption='', highlight_first=False):
    thead = ''.join(f'<th>{h}</th>' for h in headers)
    tbody = ''
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        row_class = ' class="highlight-row"' if highlight_first and i == 0 else ''
        tbody += f'<tr{row_class}>' + ''.join(f'<td>{cell}</td>' for cell in row) + '</tr>'
    cap = f'<caption>{caption}</caption>' if caption else ''
    return f'<table>{cap}<thead><tr>{thead}</tr></thead><tbody>{tbody}</tbody></table>'

  .risk-badge {{
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 2px 8px;
    border-radius: 4px;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 600;
  }}
  .risk-badge.high {{ background: #fef2f2; color: #b91c1c; }}
  .risk-badge.medium {{ background: #fffbeb; color: #b45309; }}
  .risk-badge.low {{ background: #f0fdf4; color: #15803d; }}

  /* Divider */
  .divider {{
    height: 1px;
    background: var(--border);
    margin: 32px 0;
  }}

  /* Footer */
  .report-footer {{
    background: var(--primary);
    color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7);
    padding: 30px 60px;
    font-size: 13px;

    align-items: center;

  /* Print optimizations */
  @media print {{
    .cover {{ min-height: auto; padding: 40px; }}
    .section {{ page-break-inside: avoid; }}
    .chart-container {{ page-break-inside: avoid; }}

  /* Responsive */
  @media (max-width: 768px) {{
    .kpi-grid {{ grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }}
    .chart-row {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .insight-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }}
    .rec-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .toc-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .two-col-text {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .page {{ padding: 0 20px; }}
    .cover {{ padding: 40px 20px; }}

</head>
<body>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ COVER PAGE ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="cover">

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ TABLE OF CONTENTS ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="toc">
  <h2>Table of Contents</h2>

<div class="page">

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="executive-overview">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 01</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Executive Overview</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">A synthesis of the five most critical findings from 12,343 records spanning 21 years of AI-driven workforce disruption. These insights should inform immediate strategic decisions on talent investment and reskilling.</p>
  </div>

  <!-- KPI Summary Row -->
  <div class="kpi-grid">
    <div class="kpi-card blue">
      <div class="kpi-label">Avg AI Risk Score</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{avg_risk:.2f}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Scale 0–1 across all roles</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta {'up' if risk_trend_direction == 'increasing' else 'down'}">
        {'▲' if risk_trend_direction == 'increasing' else '▼'} {risk_abs_change:.3f} vs. 2015–17 baseline
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card green">
      <div class="kpi-label">Overall Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(overall_median_salary)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Annual USD across all records</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta {'up' if salary_change > 0 else 'down'}">
        {'▲' if salary_change > 0 else '▼'} {abs(salary_change):.1f}% from 2015–17 to 2033–35
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card {'red' if at_risk_pct > 40 else 'amber'}">
      <div class="kpi-label">At-Risk Jobs (Class 0)</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{at_risk_pct:.1f}%</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Proportion facing high automation threat</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta neutral">{fmt_pct(strong_survival_pct)} in strong survival</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card teal">
      <div class="kpi-label">Avg Skill Demand Score</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{avg_skill_demand:.1f}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Scale 0–100, market-wide average</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta neutral">Top skill: {top_skill} ({top_skill_demand:.1f})</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Critical Findings -->
  <div class="callout danger">
    <div class="callout-icon">⚠</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">AI Risk Is Rising — {fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)} of Roles Are High Risk</div>
      <div class="callout-text">Average automation risk has moved from {early_risk:.3f} (2015–17) to {late_risk:.3f} (2033–35) — a {risk_trend_direction} trajectory of {risk_abs_change:.3f} points. {fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)} of all recorded roles fall in the "High Risk" category. Without active intervention, workforce displacement will accelerate through the projection horizon.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h3 style="font-size:18px; font-weight:700; color:var(--primary); margin:28px 0 16px;">Five Critical Findings</h3>

  <ul class="findings-list">
    <li>
      <div class="bullet red">1</div>
      <div><strong>Automation risk is concentrated and growing.</strong> The dataset shows a {risk_trend_direction} risk trend from {early_risk:.3f} to {late_risk:.3f} over the 2015–2035 window. <strong>{highest_risk_job}</strong> carries the highest average risk score ({highest_risk_val:.3f}), while <strong>{lowest_risk_job}</strong> remains the most resilient ({lowest_risk_val:.3f}).</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet green">2</div>
      <div><strong>Low-risk roles command a significant salary premium.</strong> Roles in the "Low Risk" category earn a median of <strong>{fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)}</strong> versus <strong>{fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}</strong> for "High Risk" roles — a <strong>{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% premium</strong>. This confirms that AI-resistant competencies are being compensated at a premium, a signal that should guide reskilling investment priorities.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet blue">3</div>
      <div><strong>Skill demand divergence is accelerating.</strong> Market demand for high-value technical skills is diverging sharply from commoditized roles. <strong>{top_skill}</strong> leads demand scoring at {top_skill_demand:.1f}/100. Skills tied to AI-adjacent work (Python, Security, AWS, Docker) hold both high demand and lower automation risk profiles.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet amber">4</div>
      <div><strong>Job survival prospects improve with experience and education.</strong> Senior-level professionals show markedly lower AI risk scores than Entry-level counterparts. PhD and Master's degree holders command higher salaries, and survival class distributions favor more educated and experienced cohorts — underscoring the value of workforce upskilling programs.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet teal">5</div>
      <div><strong>Job openings volume shifted {'upward' if openings_change_pct > 0 else 'downward'} — but composition matters.</strong> Total job openings changed by <strong>{openings_change_pct:.1f}%</strong> from the early period (2015–17) to the projected end period (2033–35). Growth is concentrated in roles with strong survival class ratings, while at-risk categories see volume compression. Geographic variation is also significant, with <strong>{highest_salary_country}</strong> maintaining the highest median compensation.</div>
    </li>
  </ul>

  <div class="chart-row" style="margin-top:28px;">
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_trend}
      <div class="chart-caption">AI risk score trending {risk_trend_direction} across the full 2015–2035 horizon. Future years (2025–2035) represent model projections.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_salary_trend}
      <div class="chart-caption">Global median salary trend in USD. Salary growth reflects both inflation and compositional shifts toward higher-skill roles.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 2: AUTOMATION RISK LANDSCAPE ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="automation-risk-landscape">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 02</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">AI Automation Risk Landscape</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Mapping automation exposure across job titles, geographies, and experience levels to identify where displacement risk is highest and where resilience is strongest.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="insight-grid">
    <div class="insight-card red">
      <div class="insight-number">{fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">High-Risk Roles</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Proportion of records with ai_risk_score > 0.6 — the threshold for significant automation exposure</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card amber">
      <div class="insight-number">{highest_risk_val:.2f}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Peak Role Risk</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">{highest_risk_job} — highest mean automation risk score across all job titles in the dataset</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card green">
      <div class="insight-number">{fmt_pct(low_risk_pct)}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Low-Risk Roles</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Roles with ai_risk_score ≤ 0.4, indicating strong resilience against near-term automation</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-container">
    {chart_risk_by_job}
    <div class="chart-caption">Mean AI risk score by job title. Red bars indicate high risk (>0.6), amber bars medium risk (0.4–0.6), green bars low risk (<0.4).</div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row">
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_country}
      <div class="chart-caption">Average AI risk score by country. Geographic variation likely reflects industry mix and automation adoption pace.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_exp}
      <div class="chart-caption">Risk score by experience level. Entry-level roles face systematically higher automation risk than Senior professionals.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout warning">
    <div class="callout-icon">ⓘ</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">Experience Level Acts as an Automation Buffer</div>
      <div class="callout-text">Entry-level workers face the highest average AI risk, reflecting the concentration of routine, codifiable tasks at the beginning of most career paths. Senior professionals — who handle ambiguity, stakeholder management, and complex judgment — show meaningfully lower risk scores. This has direct implications for onboarding and early-career development programs.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">AI Risk Score & Median Salary by Job Title</div>
    {table_html(
      ['Job Title', 'Avg AI Risk Score', 'Risk Category'],
      job_risk_table_rows,
      highlight_first=True
    )}
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">Risk & Salary by Country</div>
    {table_html(
      ['Country', 'Avg AI Risk Score', 'Median Salary (USD)'],
      country_risk_salary_rows
    )}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 3: SALARY TRENDS ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="salary-trends">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 03</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Salary Trends & Segmentation</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Compensation dynamics across experience, geography, and AI risk category — revealing where salary premiums are growing and how automation risk shapes earning potential.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="kpi-grid">
    <div class="kpi-card green">
      <div class="kpi-label">Low-Risk Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Roles with ai_risk_score ≤ 0.4</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card red">
      <div class="kpi-label">High-Risk Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Roles with ai_risk_score > 0.6</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card blue">
      <div class="kpi-label">Low/High Risk Premium</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}%</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Salary premium for low-risk roles</div>

    <div class="kpi-card teal">
      <div class="kpi-label">Highest Paying Country</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{highest_salary_country}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Median {fmt_usd(highest_salary_val)} annually</div>

  <div class="callout {'success' if salary_premium_low_vs_high > 0 else 'warning'}">
    <div class="callout-icon">💡</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">Key Insight: Automation Risk Is a Salary Discount Factor</div>
      <div class="callout-text">The data reveals a clear inverse correlation between AI risk and compensation. Low-risk roles earn <strong>{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% more</strong> at the median than high-risk roles ({fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)} vs. {fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}). This premium likely reflects a combination of scarcity value (skills harder to automate command a market premium) and selection effects (more experienced, educated workers tend to occupy lower-risk positions). Strategically, reskilling toward low-risk competencies offers a dual ROI: reduced displacement risk and improved earnings potential.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-container">
    {chart_salary_exp}
    <div class="chart-caption">Median salary by experience level over the full 2015–2035 period. The senior–entry salary gap persists and may widen as AI compresses entry-level role availability.</div>
  </div>

    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_salary_risk}

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">Risk & Salary Correlation Summary by Category</div>
    {table_html(
      ['AI Risk Category', 'Median Salary (USD)', 'Mean Survival Class', 'Record Count'],

        row['ai_risk_category'],

        fmt_num(row['count'])
      ] for _, row in risk_salary_corr.iterrows()]

</div>

  <div class="chart-container">

  <div class="callout info">

  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 05</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Job Survival & Market Outlook</h2>

  <div class="chart-row">

    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">Job Survival Rate, Risk & Salary by Role</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 6: STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="strategic-recommendations">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 06</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Strategic Recommendations</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Six data-grounded recommendations for workforce planners, talent leaders, and executives. Each is tied directly to a specific finding from the analysis above.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="rec-grid">
    <div class="rec-card">
      <div class="rec-number">1</div>
      <div class="rec-title">Prioritize Reskilling Toward Low-Risk, High-Demand Skills</div>
      <div class="rec-body">Direct reskilling investment toward skills that simultaneously score high on demand and low on AI risk — specifically Python, Security, AWS, and Docker. These competencies appear at the intersection of high market demand and structural resilience against automation.</div>
      <div class="rec-basis"><strong>Data basis:</strong> Low-risk roles earn {salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% more at the median ({fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)} vs. {fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}). Skills like {top_skill} lead demand scoring at {top_skill_demand:.1f}/100.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="rec-card">
      <div class="rec-number">2</div>
      <div class="rec-title">Protect Entry-Level Pipelines Proactively</div>
      <div class="rec-body">Entry-level roles carry the highest average AI risk scores in the dataset. Organizations must redesign early-career development programs to accelerate advancement through automation-vulnerable stages, ensuring new talent develops judgment and complexity-handling capabilities faster.</div>
      <div class="rec-basis"><strong>Data basis:</strong> Entry-level ai_risk_score significantly exceeds Senior-level risk in cross-experience analysis. Routine task concentration drives this gap.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="rec-card">
      <div class="rec-number">3</div>
      <div class="rec-title">Calibrate Compensation Strategy to Risk Profiles</div>
      <div class="rec-body">Use AI risk categorization as a compensation benchmarking input. Roles at High Risk of automation should be benchmarked against their reskilled or transitioned equivalents, not their current market rate, to avoid overpaying for roles with shrinking longevity while underpaying for resilient skills under competitive pressure.</div>
      <div class="rec-basis"><strong>Data basis:</strong> {fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)} of roles are High Risk. Low-risk roles command a {salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% median premium — a structural signal, not noise.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="rec-card">
      <div class="rec-number">4</div>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate AI Job Market Impact Report from data.csv"""

import pandas as pd
import json
import math
from collections import defaultdict

# ── Load Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ── Helper: number formatting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_num(n, decimals=0):
    if decimals == 0:
        return f"{int(round(n)):,}"
    return f"{n:,.{decimals}f}"

def fmt_pct(n, decimals=1):
    return f"{n:.{decimals}f}%"

def fmt_usd(n):
    return f"${int(round(n)):,}"

# ── Data Aggregations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# 1. Average AI Risk Score by Year
risk_by_year = df.groupby('year')['ai_risk_score'].mean().reset_index()
risk_by_year.columns = ['year', 'avg_risk']

# 2. Median Salary by Year
salary_by_year = df.groupby('year')['salary'].median().reset_index()
salary_by_year.columns = ['year', 'median_salary']

# 3. Job Openings by Year
openings_by_year = df.groupby('year')['job_openings'].sum().reset_index()

# 4. Skill Demand by Year
skill_demand_by_year = df.groupby('year')['skill_demand_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 5. Risk by Job Title (top 10)
risk_by_job = df.groupby('job_title')['ai_risk_score'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()
risk_by_job.columns = ['job_title', 'avg_risk']

# 6. Risk by Country (all)
risk_by_country = df.groupby('country')['ai_risk_score'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()

# 7. Salary by Country
salary_by_country = df.groupby('country')['salary'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()

# 8. Salary by Experience Level over time
salary_exp_year = df.groupby(['year', 'experience_level'])['salary'].median().reset_index()

# 9. Salary by Risk Category
salary_risk = df.groupby('ai_risk_category')['salary'].median().reset_index()

# 10. Job Survival class distribution by year
survival_dist = df.groupby(['year', 'job_survival_class']).size().reset_index(name='count')
total_by_year = df.groupby('year').size().reset_index(name='total')
survival_dist = survival_dist.merge(total_by_year, on='year')
survival_dist['pct'] = survival_dist['count'] / survival_dist['total'] * 100

# 11. Top skills by demand
skill_demand = df.groupby('primary_skill').agg(
    avg_demand=('skill_demand_score', 'mean'),
    avg_risk=('ai_risk_score', 'mean'),
    survival_rate=('job_survival_class', lambda x: (x >= 1).mean() * 100)
).reset_index().sort_values('avg_demand', ascending=False)

# 12. Risk category distribution
risk_cat_dist = df.groupby('ai_risk_category').size().reset_index(name='count')
risk_cat_dist['pct'] = risk_cat_dist['count'] / len(df) * 100

# 13. Survival by job title
survival_by_job = df.groupby('job_title').agg(
    survival_rate=('job_survival_class', lambda x: (x >= 1).mean() * 100),
    avg_risk=('ai_risk_score', 'mean'),
    avg_salary=('salary', 'median')
).reset_index().sort_values('survival_rate', ascending=False)

# 14. Risk by experience level
risk_by_exp = df.groupby('experience_level')['ai_risk_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 15. Salary by education
salary_by_edu = df.groupby('education_level')['salary'].median().reset_index().sort_values('salary', ascending=False)

# 16. Skill demand over time for top skills
top_skills = skill_demand.head(5)['primary_skill'].tolist()
skill_trend = df[df['primary_skill'].isin(top_skills)].groupby(['year', 'primary_skill'])['skill_demand_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 17. High risk jobs salary vs survival
risk_salary_corr = df.groupby('ai_risk_category').agg(
    median_salary=('salary', 'median'),
    survival_class_mean=('job_survival_class', 'mean'),
    count=('job_title', 'count')
).reset_index()

# 18. Job openings by job title
openings_by_job = df.groupby('job_title')['job_openings'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index().head(10)

# 19. Survival class over future years
future_df = df[df['year'] >= 2025]
hist_df = df[df['year'] < 2025]

# 20. Overall KPIs
total_records = len(df)
avg_risk = df['ai_risk_score'].mean()
overall_median_salary = df['salary'].median()
survival_rate_overall = (df['job_survival_class'] >= 1).mean() * 100
avg_skill_demand = df['skill_demand_score'].mean()
total_openings = df['job_openings'].sum()

# Risk trend: first 3 years vs last 3 years
early_risk = df[df['year'] <= 2017]['ai_risk_score'].mean()
late_risk = df[df['year'] >= 2033]['ai_risk_score'].mean()
risk_change = (late_risk - early_risk) / early_risk * 100

# Salary trend
early_salary = df[df['year'] <= 2017]['salary'].median()
late_salary = df[df['year'] >= 2033]['salary'].median()
salary_change = (late_salary - early_salary) / early_salary * 100

print(f"Records: {total_records}")
print(f"Avg AI Risk: {avg_risk:.3f}")
print(f"Median Salary: {overall_median_salary:.0f}")
print(f"Survival Rate: {survival_rate_overall:.1f}%")
print(f"Risk change 2015-17 vs 2033-35: {risk_change:.1f}%")
print(f"Salary change: {salary_change:.1f}%")
print(f"\nRisk by job:\n{risk_by_job}")
print(f"\nTop skills:\n{skill_demand.head(8)}")
print(f"\nRisk by country:\n{risk_by_country}")
print(f"\nSalary vs risk:\n{risk_salary_corr}")
print(f"\nSurvival by job:\n{survival_by_job}")

# ── SVG Chart generators ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def svg_line_chart(data_series, width=700, height=320, title='', colors=None, x_label='', y_label='',
                   y_format='auto', show_legend=True):
    """Multi-line SVG chart. data_series = {label: [(x, y), ...]}"""
    if colors is None:
        colors = ['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#dc2626', '#d97706', '#7c3aed', '#0891b2']

    pad_left = 75
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 55
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    all_x = sorted(set(x for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts))
    all_y = [y for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts]

    if not all_x or not all_y:
        return ''

    x_min, x_max = min(all_x), max(all_x)
    y_min_raw, y_max_raw = min(all_y), max(all_y)
    y_padding = (y_max_raw - y_min_raw) * 0.1 or y_max_raw * 0.1
    y_min = y_min_raw - y_padding
    y_max = y_max_raw + y_padding

    def px(x_val):
        if x_max == x_min:
            return pad_left + chart_w / 2
        return pad_left + (x_val - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * chart_w

    def py(y_val):
        if y_max == y_min:
            return pad_top + chart_h / 2
        return pad_top + (1 - (y_val - y_min) / (y_max - y_min)) * chart_h

    # Y grid lines
    n_grid = 5
    grid_lines = ''
    y_labels_svg = ''
    for i in range(n_grid + 1):
        y_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / n_grid
        y_pos = py(y_val)
        grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
        if y_format == 'pct':
            label = f'{y_val:.1f}%'
        elif y_format == 'usd':
            label = f'${y_val/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'k':
            label = f'{y_val/1000:.0f}K'
        elif y_format == 'M':
            label = f'{y_val/1e6:.1f}M'
        else:
            label = f'{y_val:.2f}' if y_val < 10 else f'{int(y_val):,}'
        y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{label}</text>'

    # X axis labels
    x_labels_svg = ''
    step = max(1, len(all_x) // 8)
    for i, x_val in enumerate(all_x):
        if i % step == 0 or x_val == all_x[-1]:
            x_pos = px(x_val)
            x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_pos:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+20}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{x_val}</text>'

    # Lines
    paths = ''
    for idx, (label, pts) in enumerate(data_series.items()):
        color = colors[idx % len(colors)]
        pts_sorted = sorted(pts, key=lambda p: p[0])
        d = ' '.join(f'{"M" if i==0 else "L"}{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for i, (x, y) in enumerate(pts_sorted))
        paths += f'<path d="{d}" fill="none" stroke="{color}" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/>'
        # Dots at each point
        for x, y in pts_sorted:
            paths += f'<circle cx="{px(x):.1f}" cy="{py(y):.1f}" r="3" fill="{color}"/>'

    # Legend
    legend_svg = ''
    if show_legend and len(data_series) > 1:
        lx = pad_left
        for idx, label in enumerate(data_series.keys()):
            color = colors[idx % len(colors)]
            legend_svg += f'''<rect x="{lx}" y="{height-18}" width="12" height="12" fill="{color}" rx="2"/>
            <text x="{lx+16}" y="{height-7}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{label}</text>'''
            lx += len(label) * 7 + 30

    # Title
    title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

    return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {paths}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="{pad_left}" y="{height-4}" font-size="10" fill="#9ca3af">{x_label}</text>
</svg>'''


def svg_bar_chart(labels, values, width=700, height=320, title='', color='#2563eb',
                  colors=None, y_format='auto', horizontal=False, show_values=True):
    """Single-series bar chart."""
    pad_left = 75 if not horizontal else 150

            return f'{v/1000:.1f}K'

            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h - bar_h
            bars += f'<rect x="{x_center - bar_w/2:.1f}" y="{y_pos:.1f}" width="{bar_w:.1f}" height="{bar_h:.1f}" fill="{bar_colors[i % len(bar_colors)]}" rx="3"/>'
            if show_values:
                bars += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{y_pos - 4:.1f}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{fmt_val(val)}</text>'
            # X labels - wrap long labels
            lbl_str = str(lbl)
            if len(lbl_str) > 12:
                words = lbl_str.split()
                if len(words) > 1:
                    mid = len(words) // 2
                    line1 = ' '.join(words[:mid])

                    x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#6b7280">{line1}</text>'
                    x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{x_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+29}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#6b7280">{line2}</text>'
                else:

        # Y grid

            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h * (1 - i / 5)
            grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
            y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{fmt_val(y_val)}</text>'

        title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

        return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>

    else:
        # horizontal

        for i, (lbl, val) in enumerate(zip(labels, values)):

            if show_values:
                bars += f'<text x="{pad_left + bar_len + 5:.1f}" y="{y_center + 4:.1f}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{fmt_val(val)}</text>'
            lbl_str = str(lbl)[:22]
            y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left - 6}" y="{y_center + 4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{lbl_str}</text>'

    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right

        for si, (sname, vals) in enumerate(series_data.items()):

            x_pos = group_center - (n_series / 2 * bar_w) + si * bar_w
            y_pos = pad_top + chart_h - bar_h
            bars += f'<rect x="{x_pos:.1f}" y="{y_pos:.1f}" width="{bar_w:.1f}" height="{bar_h:.1f}" fill="{color}" rx="2"/>'

        lbl = str(group)
        x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{group_center:.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+16}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{lbl}</text>'

    # Y grid
    grid_lines = ''
    y_labels_svg = ''
    for i in range(6):
        y_val = y_min + (y_max - y_min) * i / 5

  {grid_lines}
  {bars}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''


def svg_stacked_area(data_series, width=700, height=320, title='', colors=None, y_format='pct', x_label=''):
    """Stacked area chart. data_series = {label: [(x, y), ...]} where y are proportions."""
    if colors is None:
        colors = ['#dc2626', '#d97706', '#16a34a']

    pad_left = 60
    pad_right = 30
    pad_top = 50
    pad_bottom = 55
    chart_w = width - pad_left - pad_right
    chart_h = height - pad_top - pad_bottom

    all_x = sorted(set(x for pts in data_series.values() for x, y in pts))
    if not all_x:
        return ''
    x_min, x_max = min(all_x), max(all_x)

    def px(x_val):
        if x_max == x_min:
            return pad_left + chart_w / 2
        return pad_left + (x_val - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * chart_w

    # Build stacked values
    series_names = list(data_series.keys())
    # For each x, get cumulative sums
    x_vals_map = defaultdict(dict)
    for sname, pts in data_series.items():
        for x, y in pts:
            x_vals_map[x][sname] = y

    paths_svg = ''
    for si, sname in enumerate(series_names):
        color = colors[si % len(colors)]
        # compute bottom and top stacks
        top_pts = []
        bot_pts = []
        for x in all_x:
            cum_top = sum(x_vals_map[x].get(s, 0) for s in series_names[:si+1])
            cum_bot = sum(x_vals_map[x].get(s, 0) for s in series_names[:si])
            top_pts.append((x, cum_top))
            bot_pts.append((x, cum_bot))

        def py(y_val):
            return pad_top + (1 - y_val / 100) * chart_h

        # Forward top, backward bottom
        forward = ' '.join(f'{"M" if i==0 else "L"}{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for i, (x, y) in enumerate(top_pts))
        backward = ' '.join(f'L{px(x):.1f},{py(y):.1f}' for x, y in reversed(bot_pts))
        d = f'{forward} {backward} Z'
        paths_svg += f'<path d="{d}" fill="{color}" opacity="0.8"/>'

    # Y labels
    y_labels_svg = ''
    grid_lines = ''
    for i in range(6):
        y_val = i * 20
        y_pos = pad_top + chart_h * (1 - y_val / 100)
        grid_lines += f'<line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{y_pos:.1f}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{y_pos:.1f}" stroke="#e5e7eb" stroke-width="1"/>'
        y_labels_svg += f'<text x="{pad_left-6}" y="{y_pos+4:.1f}" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{y_val}%</text>'

    # X labels
    x_labels_svg = ''
    step = max(1, len(all_x) // 8)
    for i, x_val in enumerate(all_x):
        if i % step == 0 or x_val == all_x[-1]:
            x_labels_svg += f'<text x="{px(x_val):.1f}" y="{pad_top+chart_h+20}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#6b7280">{x_val}</text>'

    # Legend
    legend_svg = ''
    lx = pad_left
    for si, sname in enumerate(series_names):
        color = colors[si % len(colors)]
        legend_svg += f'''<rect x="{lx}" y="{height-18}" width="12" height="12" fill="{color}" rx="2" opacity="0.8"/>
        <text x="{lx+16}" y="{height-7}" font-size="11" fill="#374151">{sname}</text>'''
        lx += len(sname) * 7 + 30

    title_svg = f'<text x="{width//2}" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#111827">{title}</text>' if title else ''

    return f'''<svg width="{width}" height="{height}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;">
  {title_svg}
  <rect x="{pad_left}" y="{pad_top}" width="{chart_w}" height="{chart_h}" fill="#f9fafb" rx="4"/>
  {grid_lines}
  {paths_svg}
  {y_labels_svg}
  {x_labels_svg}
  {legend_svg}
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top}" x2="{pad_left}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <line x1="{pad_left}" y1="{pad_top+chart_h}" x2="{pad_left+chart_w}" y2="{pad_top+chart_h}" stroke="#d1d5db" stroke-width="1.5"/>
</svg>'''

    for i, row in enumerate(rows):

    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 12px;
    overflow: hidden;
    margin-bottom: 24px;
  }}
  .table-title {{
    padding: 16px 20px;
    font-size: 15px;
    font-weight: 700;
    color: var(--primary);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
    background: #f8fafc;
  }}
  table {{
    width: 100%;
    border-collapse: collapse;
    font-size: 13.5px;
  }}
  table caption {{
    font-size: 14px;
    font-weight: 600;
    color: var(--primary);
    padding: 14px 20px;
    text-align: left;
    background: #f8fafc;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  }}
  th {{
    background: #f1f5f9;
    padding: 11px 16px;
    text-align: left;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 700;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.6px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  }}
  td {{
    padding: 10px 16px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #f1f5f9;
    color: var(--text);
  }}
  tr:last-child td {{ border-bottom: none; }}
  tr:hover td {{ background: #f8fafc; }}
  tr.highlight-row td {{
    background: #eff6ff;
    font-weight: 600;
  }}

  /* Callout Boxes */
  .callout {{
    border-radius: 10px;
    padding: 18px 22px;
    margin-bottom: 20px;
    display: flex;
    gap: 14px;
    align-items: flex-start;
  }}
  .callout.info {{
    background: #eff6ff;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--primary-light);
  }}
  .callout.success {{
    background: #f0fdf4;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--success);
  }}
  .callout.warning {{
    background: #fffbeb;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--warning);
  }}
  .callout.danger {{
    background: #fef2f2;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--danger);
  }}
  .callout-icon {{
    font-size: 18px;
    flex-shrink: 0;
    margin-top: 1px;
  }}
  .callout-content {{ flex: 1; }}
  .callout-title {{
    font-size: 14px;
    font-weight: 700;
    margin-bottom: 4px;
  }}
  .callout.info .callout-title {{ color: #1d4ed8; }}
  .callout.success .callout-title {{ color: #15803d; }}
  .callout.warning .callout-title {{ color: #b45309; }}
  .callout.danger .callout-title {{ color: #b91c1c; }}
  .callout-text {{
    font-size: 14px;
    line-height: 1.6;
    color: var(--text);
  }}

  /* Insight boxes */
  .insight-grid {{
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
    gap: 16px;
    margin-bottom: 24px;
  }}
  .insight-card {{
    background: var(--surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 10px;
    padding: 18px;
  }}
  .insight-number {{
    font-size: 36px;
    font-weight: 800;
    line-height: 1;
    margin-bottom: 6px;
  }}
  .insight-card.blue .insight-number {{ color: var(--primary-light); }}
  .insight-card.green .insight-number {{ color: var(--success); }}
  .insight-card.red .insight-number {{ color: var(--danger); }}
  .insight-card.amber .insight-number {{ color: var(--warning); }}
  .insight-card.teal .insight-number {{ color: var(--accent); }}
  .insight-label {{
    font-size: 13px;
    font-weight: 600;
    color: var(--text);
    margin-bottom: 4px;
  }}
  .insight-desc {{
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    line-height: 1.5;
  }}

  /* Findings list */
  .findings-list {{
    list-style: none;
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
  }}
  .findings-list li {{
    display: flex;
    gap: 12px;
    padding: 14px 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #f1f5f9;
    font-size: 14.5px;
    line-height: 1.6;
  }}
  .findings-list li:last-child {{ border-bottom: none; }}
  .findings-list .bullet {{
    width: 22px; height: 22px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
    font-size: 11px; font-weight: 800;
    flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 1px;
  }}
  .findings-list .bullet.red {{ background: #fef2f2; color: var(--danger); }}
  .findings-list .bullet.green {{ background: #f0fdf4; color: var(--success); }}
  .findings-list .bullet.blue {{ background: #eff6ff; color: var(--primary-light); }}
  .findings-list .bullet.amber {{ background: #fffbeb; color: var(--warning); }}
  .findings-list .bullet.teal {{ background: #ecfeff; color: var(--accent); }}

  /* Recommendations */
  .rec-grid {{
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
    gap: 20px;
    margin-top: 24px;
  }}
  .rec-card {{
    background: var(--surface);
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius: 12px;
    padding: 24px;
    position: relative;
  }}
  .rec-number {{
    position: absolute;
    top: -12px; left: 20px;
    width: 28px; height: 28px;
    background: var(--primary);
    color: white;
    border-radius: 50%;
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
    font-size: 13px; font-weight: 800;
  }}
  .rec-title {{
    font-size: 16px;
    font-weight: 700;
    color: var(--primary);
    margin-bottom: 10px;
    margin-top: 6px;
  }}
  .rec-body {{
    font-size: 14px;
    color: var(--text);
    line-height: 1.65;
  }}
  .rec-basis {{
    margin-top: 12px;
    font-size: 12px;
    color: var(--text-muted);
    background: #f8fafc;
    border-radius: 6px;
    padding: 8px 12px;
    border-left: 3px solid var(--accent);
  }}
  .rec-basis strong {{ color: var(--accent); }}

  /* Two-col text layout */
  .two-col-text {{
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
    gap: 32px;
    margin-bottom: 24px;
  }}

  /* Risk badge */
  .risk-badge {{
    display: inline-block;
    padding: 2px 8px;
    border-radius: 4px;
    font-size: 12px;
    font-weight: 600;
  }}
  .risk-badge.high {{ background: #fef2f2; color: #b91c1c; }}
  .risk-badge.medium {{ background: #fffbeb; color: #b45309; }}
  .risk-badge.low {{ background: #f0fdf4; color: #15803d; }}

  /* Divider */
  .divider {{
    height: 1px;
    background: var(--border);
    margin: 32px 0;
  }}

  /* Footer */
  .report-footer {{
    background: var(--primary);
    color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7);
    padding: 30px 60px;
    font-size: 13px;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    align-items: center;
  }}
  .report-footer strong {{ color: white; }}

  /* Print optimizations */
  @media print {{
    .cover {{ min-height: auto; padding: 40px; }}
    .section {{ page-break-inside: avoid; }}
    .chart-container {{ page-break-inside: avoid; }}
  }}

  /* Responsive */
  @media (max-width: 768px) {{
    .kpi-grid {{ grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }}
    .chart-row {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .insight-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }}
    .rec-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .toc-grid {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .two-col-text {{ grid-template-columns: 1fr; }}
    .page {{ padding: 0 20px; }}
    .cover {{ padding: 40px 20px; }}
    .cover h1 {{ font-size: 28px; }}
  }}
</style>
</head>
<body>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ COVER PAGE ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="cover">
  <div class="cover-badge">Workforce Strategy Report · April 2026</div>
  <h1>AI Impact on the<br><span>Global Job Market</span></h1>
  <p class="subtitle">Risk, Salary & Skills Trend Analysis · 2015–2035</p>
  <div class="cover-meta">
    <div class="cover-meta-item">
      <div class="label">Data Coverage</div>
      <div class="value">12,343 Records · 2015–2035</div>
    </div>
    <div class="cover-meta-item">
      <div class="label">Geography</div>
      <div class="value">{len(df['country'].unique())} Countries</div>
    </div>
    <div class="cover-meta-item">
      <div class="label">Roles Analyzed</div>
      <div class="value">{len(df['job_title'].unique())} Job Titles</div>
    </div>
    <div class="cover-meta-item">
      <div class="label">Audience</div>
      <div class="value">Executive Leadership & Workforce Strategy</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ TABLE OF CONTENTS ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="toc">
  <h2>Table of Contents</h2>
  <div class="toc-grid">
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">1</div><div class="toc-text">Executive Overview</div></div>
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">2</div><div class="toc-text">AI Automation Risk Landscape</div></div>
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">3</div><div class="toc-text">Salary Trends & Segmentation</div></div>
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">4</div><div class="toc-text">Skills Demand & Future-Proofing</div></div>
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">5</div><div class="toc-text">Job Survival & Market Outlook</div></div>
    <div class="toc-item"><div class="toc-num">6</div><div class="toc-text">Strategic Recommendations</div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="page">

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="executive-overview">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 01</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Executive Overview</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">A synthesis of the five most critical findings from 12,343 records spanning 21 years of AI-driven workforce disruption. These insights should inform immediate strategic decisions on talent investment and reskilling.</p>
  </div>

  <!-- KPI Summary Row -->
  <div class="kpi-grid">
    <div class="kpi-card blue">
      <div class="kpi-label">Avg AI Risk Score</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{avg_risk:.2f}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Scale 0–1 across all roles</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta {'up' if risk_trend_direction == 'increasing' else 'down'}">
        {'▲' if risk_trend_direction == 'increasing' else '▼'} {risk_abs_change:.3f} vs. 2015–17 baseline
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card green">
      <div class="kpi-label">Overall Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(overall_median_salary)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Annual USD across all records</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta {'up' if salary_change > 0 else 'down'}">
        {'▲' if salary_change > 0 else '▼'} {abs(salary_change):.1f}% from 2015–17 to 2033–35
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card {'red' if at_risk_pct > 40 else 'amber'}">
      <div class="kpi-label">At-Risk Jobs (Class 0)</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{at_risk_pct:.1f}%</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Proportion facing high automation threat</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta neutral">{fmt_pct(strong_survival_pct)} in strong survival</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card teal">
      <div class="kpi-label">Avg Skill Demand Score</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{avg_skill_demand:.1f}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Scale 0–100, market-wide average</div>
      <div class="kpi-delta neutral">Top skill: {top_skill} ({top_skill_demand:.1f})</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Critical Findings -->
  <div class="callout danger">
    <div class="callout-icon">⚠</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">AI Risk Is Rising — {fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)} of Roles Are High Risk</div>
      <div class="callout-text">Average automation risk has moved from {early_risk:.3f} (2015–17) to {late_risk:.3f} (2033–35) — a {risk_trend_direction} trajectory of {risk_abs_change:.3f} points. {fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)} of all recorded roles fall in the "High Risk" category. Without active intervention, workforce displacement will accelerate through the projection horizon.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h3 style="font-size:18px; font-weight:700; color:var(--primary); margin:28px 0 16px;">Five Critical Findings</h3>

  <ul class="findings-list">
    <li>
      <div class="bullet red">1</div>
      <div><strong>Automation risk is concentrated and growing.</strong> The dataset shows a {risk_trend_direction} risk trend from {early_risk:.3f} to {late_risk:.3f} over the 2015–2035 window. <strong>{highest_risk_job}</strong> carries the highest average risk score ({highest_risk_val:.3f}), while <strong>{lowest_risk_job}</strong> remains the most resilient ({lowest_risk_val:.3f}).</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet green">2</div>
      <div><strong>Low-risk roles command a significant salary premium.</strong> Roles in the "Low Risk" category earn a median of <strong>{fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)}</strong> versus <strong>{fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}</strong> for "High Risk" roles — a <strong>{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% premium</strong>. This confirms that AI-resistant competencies are being compensated at a premium, a signal that should guide reskilling investment priorities.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet blue">3</div>
      <div><strong>Skill demand divergence is accelerating.</strong> Market demand for high-value technical skills is diverging sharply from commoditized roles. <strong>{top_skill}</strong> leads demand scoring at {top_skill_demand:.1f}/100. Skills tied to AI-adjacent work (Python, Security, AWS, Docker) hold both high demand and lower automation risk profiles.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet amber">4</div>
      <div><strong>Job survival prospects improve with experience and education.</strong> Senior-level professionals show markedly lower AI risk scores than Entry-level counterparts. PhD and Master's degree holders command higher salaries, and survival class distributions favor more educated and experienced cohorts — underscoring the value of workforce upskilling programs.</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div class="bullet teal">5</div>
      <div><strong>Job openings volume shifted {'upward' if openings_change_pct > 0 else 'downward'} — but composition matters.</strong> Total job openings changed by <strong>{openings_change_pct:.1f}%</strong> from the early period (2015–17) to the projected end period (2033–35). Growth is concentrated in roles with strong survival class ratings, while at-risk categories see volume compression. Geographic variation is also significant, with <strong>{highest_salary_country}</strong> maintaining the highest median compensation.</div>
    </li>
  </ul>

  <div class="chart-row" style="margin-top:28px;">
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_trend}
      <div class="chart-caption">AI risk score trending {risk_trend_direction} across the full 2015–2035 horizon. Future years (2025–2035) represent model projections.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_salary_trend}
      <div class="chart-caption">Global median salary trend in USD. Salary growth reflects both inflation and compositional shifts toward higher-skill roles.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 2: AUTOMATION RISK LANDSCAPE ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="automation-risk-landscape">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 02</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">AI Automation Risk Landscape</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Mapping automation exposure across job titles, geographies, and experience levels to identify where displacement risk is highest and where resilience is strongest.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="insight-grid">
    <div class="insight-card red">
      <div class="insight-number">{fmt_pct(high_risk_pct)}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">High-Risk Roles</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Proportion of records with ai_risk_score > 0.6 — the threshold for significant automation exposure</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card amber">
      <div class="insight-number">{highest_risk_val:.2f}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Peak Role Risk</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">{highest_risk_job} — highest mean automation risk score across all job titles in the dataset</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card green">
      <div class="insight-number">{fmt_pct(low_risk_pct)}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Low-Risk Roles</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Roles with ai_risk_score ≤ 0.4, indicating strong resilience against near-term automation</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-container">
    {chart_risk_by_job}
    <div class="chart-caption">Mean AI risk score by job title. Red bars indicate high risk (>0.6), amber bars medium risk (0.4–0.6), green bars low risk (<0.4).</div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row">
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_country}
      <div class="chart-caption">Average AI risk score by country. Geographic variation likely reflects industry mix and automation adoption pace.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_risk_exp}
      <div class="chart-caption">Risk score by experience level. Entry-level roles face systematically higher automation risk than Senior professionals.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout warning">
    <div class="callout-icon">ⓘ</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">Experience Level Acts as an Automation Buffer</div>
      <div class="callout-text">Entry-level workers face the highest average AI risk, reflecting the concentration of routine, codifiable tasks at the beginning of most career paths. Senior professionals — who handle ambiguity, stakeholder management, and complex judgment — show meaningfully lower risk scores. This has direct implications for onboarding and early-career development programs.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">AI Risk Score & Median Salary by Job Title</div>
    {table_html(
      ['Job Title', 'Avg AI Risk Score', 'Risk Category'],
      job_risk_table_rows,
      highlight_first=True
    )}
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">Risk & Salary by Country</div>
    {table_html(
      ['Country', 'Avg AI Risk Score', 'Median Salary (USD)'],
      country_risk_salary_rows
    )}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 3: SALARY TRENDS ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="salary-trends">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 03</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Salary Trends & Segmentation</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Compensation dynamics across experience, geography, and AI risk category — revealing where salary premiums are growing and how automation risk shapes earning potential.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="kpi-grid">
    <div class="kpi-card green">
      <div class="kpi-label">Low-Risk Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Roles with ai_risk_score ≤ 0.4</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card red">
      <div class="kpi-label">High-Risk Median Salary</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Roles with ai_risk_score > 0.6</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card blue">
      <div class="kpi-label">Low/High Risk Premium</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}%</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Salary premium for low-risk roles</div>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card teal">
      <div class="kpi-label">Highest Paying Country</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">{highest_salary_country}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">Median {fmt_usd(highest_salary_val)} annually</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout {'success' if salary_premium_low_vs_high > 0 else 'warning'}">
    <div class="callout-icon">💡</div>
    <div class="callout-content">
      <div class="callout-title">Key Insight: Automation Risk Is a Salary Discount Factor</div>
      <div class="callout-text">The data reveals a clear inverse correlation between AI risk and compensation. Low-risk roles earn <strong>{salary_premium_low_vs_high:.1f}% more</strong> at the median than high-risk roles ({fmt_usd(low_risk_sal)} vs. {fmt_usd(high_risk_sal)}). This premium likely reflects a combination of scarcity value (skills harder to automate command a market premium) and selection effects (more experienced, educated workers tend to occupy lower-risk positions). Strategically, reskilling toward low-risk competencies offers a dual ROI: reduced displacement risk and improved earnings potential.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-container">
    {chart_salary_exp}
    <div class="chart-caption">Median salary by experience level over the full 2015–2035 period. The senior–entry salary gap persists and may widen as AI compresses entry-level role availability.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row">
    <div class="chart-container">
      {chart_salary_risk}
      <div class="chart-caption">Median annual salary (USD) by AI risk category. The stepwise salary decline from Low to High Risk confirms compensation-risk correlation.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-container" style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; padding:28px 24px;">
      <h3 style="font-size:16px; font-weight:700; color:var(--primary); margin-bottom:16px;">Salary by Education Level</h3>
      {table_html(['Education Level', 'Median Salary (USD)'], edu_salary_rows)}
      <p style="font-size:13px; color:var(--text-muted); margin-top:12px; font-style:italic;">Advanced degrees correlate with higher compensation, consistent with their lower average AI risk profiles.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="table-container">
    <div class="table-title">Risk & Salary Correlation Summary by Category</div>
    {table_html(
      ['AI Risk Category', 'Median Salary (USD)', 'Mean Survival Class', 'Record Count'],
      [[
        row['ai_risk_category'],
        fmt_usd(row['median_salary']),
        f"{row['survival_class_mean']:.2f}",
        fmt_num(row['count'])
      ] for _, row in risk_salary_corr.iterrows()]
    )}
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ═══════════════════════════ SECTION 4: SKILLS DEMAND ═══════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section" id="skills-demand-analysis">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div class="section-tag">Section 04</div>
    <h2 class="section-title">Skills Demand & Future-Proofing</h2>
    <p class="section-lead">Identifying which skills command the highest market demand, how demand is evolving over time, and which competencies offer the strongest protection against automation.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="insight-grid">
    <div class="insight-card blue">
      <div class="insight-number">{top_skill}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Highest Demand Skill</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Leads market demand at {top_skill_demand:.1f}/100 average demand score</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card green">
      <div class="insight-number">{len(df['primary_skill'].unique())}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Distinct Skills Tracked</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Unique primary skill categories across all records in the dataset</div>
    </div>
    <div class="insight-card teal">
      <div class="insight-number">{avg_skill_demand:.0f}</div>
      <div class="insight-label">Market-Wide Avg Demand</div>
      <div class="insight-desc">Mean skill demand score (0–100) across all roles and years</div>
    </div>
  </div>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate AI Job Market Impact Report from data.csv"""

import pandas as pd

import math
from collections import defaultdict

# ── Load Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# ── Helper: number formatting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
def fmt_num(n, decimals=0):
    if decimals == 0:
        return f"{int(round(n)):,}"
    return f"{n:,.{decimals}f}"

def fmt_pct(n, decimals=1):
    return f"{n:.{decimals}f}%"

def fmt_usd(n):
    return f"${int(round(n)):,}"

# ── Data Aggregations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# 1. Average AI Risk Score by Year
risk_by_year = df.groupby('year')['ai_risk_score'].mean().reset_index()
risk_by_year.columns = ['year', 'avg_risk']

# 2. Median Salary by Year
salary_by_year = df.groupby('year')['salary'].median().reset_index()
salary_by_year.columns = ['year', 'median_salary']

# 3. Job Openings by Year
openings_by_year = df.groupby('year')['job_openings'].sum().reset_index()

# 4. Skill Demand by Year
skill_demand_by_year = df.groupby('year')['skill_demand_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 5. Risk by Job Title (top 10)
risk_by_job = df.groupby('job_title')['ai_risk_score'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()
risk_by_job.columns = ['job_title', 'avg_risk']

# 6. Risk by Country (all)
risk_by_country = df.groupby('country')['ai_risk_score'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()

# 7. Salary by Country
salary_by_country = df.groupby('country')['salary'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()

# 8. Salary by Experience Level over time
salary_exp_year = df.groupby(['year', 'experience_level'])['salary'].median().reset_index()

# 9. Salary by Risk Category
salary_risk = df.groupby('ai_risk_category')['salary'].median().reset_index()

# 10. Job Survival class distribution by year
survival_dist = df.groupby(['year', 'job_survival_class']).size().reset_index(name='count')
total_by_year = df.groupby('year').size().reset_index(name='total')
survival_dist = survival_dist.merge(total_by_year, on='year')
survival_dist['pct'] = survival_dist['count'] / survival_dist['total'] * 100

# 11. Top skills by demand
skill_demand = df.groupby('primary_skill').agg(
    avg_demand=('skill_demand_score', 'mean'),
    avg_risk=('ai_risk_score', 'mean'),
    survival_rate=('job_survival_class', lambda x: (x >= 1).mean() * 100)
).reset_index().sort_values('avg_demand', ascending=False)

# 12. Risk category distribution
risk_cat_dist = df.groupby('ai_risk_category').size().reset_index(name='count')
risk_cat_dist['pct'] = risk_cat_dist['count'] / len(df) * 100

# 13. Survival by job title
survival_by_job = df.groupby('job_title').agg(
    survival_rate=('job_survival_class', lambda x: (x >= 1).mean() * 100),
    avg_risk=('ai_risk_score', 'mean'),
    avg_salary=('salary', 'median')
).reset_index().sort_values('survival_rate', ascending=False)

# 14. Risk by experience level
risk_by_exp = df.groupby('experience_level')['ai_risk_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 15. Salary by education
salary_by_edu = df.groupby('education_level')['salary'].median().reset_index().sort_values('salary', ascending=False)

# 16. Skill demand over time for top skills

skill_trend = df[df['primary_skill'].isin(top_skills)].groupby(['year', 'primary_skill'])['skill_demand_score'].mean().reset_index()

# 17. High risk jobs salary vs survival
risk_salary_corr = df.groupby('ai_risk_category').agg(
    median_salary=('salary', 'median'),

    count=('job_title', 'count')
).reset_index()

# 18. Job openings by job title
openings_by_job = df.groupby('job_title')['job_openings'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index().head(10)

# 19. Survival class over future years
future_df = df[df['year'] >= 2025]
hist_df = df[df['year'] < 2025]

# 20. Overall KPIs
total_records = len(df)
avg_risk = df['ai_risk_score'].mean()
overall_median_salary = df['salary'].median()
survival_rate_overall = (df['job_survival_class'] >= 1).mean() * 100
avg_skill_demand = df['skill_demand_score'].mean()
total_openings = df['job_openings'].sum()

# Risk trend: first 3 years vs last 3 years
early_risk = df[df['year'] <= 2017]['ai_risk_score'].mean()
late_risk = df[df['year'] >= 2033]['ai_risk_score'].mean()

# Salary trend
